# Naming and copy

> Settled 2026-09-09; § 1 reversed by the redesign onto noddo on 2026-11-04 (the design system's
> SPEC § 1). Answers `analysis/ui/NAMING_AND_COPY.md` § 2 and the naming half of the tabs question in
> `analysis/ui/NAVIGATION.md` (removed there once built).

## 1. Sentence case, everywhere

Every user-facing label is **sentence case**: buttons, menu items, column headers, tab labels, page
titles, dialog titles, field labels, chip text, export headers and sheet names.

`Add office`, `Show archived`, `Delete profile`, `Assigned people`, `Job catalog`, `Last updated`.

Capitals stay only on **proper names**: people, other companies' products (`Google`, `Okta`,
`Microsoft`), days and months, acronyms (`HR`, `SSO`, `CSV`), and the product's own role names (`HR
Admin`, `System Owner`), which are names of things a company has. The product's own name is always
lower case — **noddo**, also at the start of a sentence.

Until 2026-11-04 the rule was Title Case; the noddo design system reversed it, and the whole product
was converted in one pass (about 700 labels; `HISTORY.md` § "The redesign onto noddo"). What counts as
a label did not change, and the one rule that matters is the same as before: **one convention, not a
per-module preference**.

**Sentences are sentences.** Page descriptions, helper text, empty-state copy, dialog bodies, error
messages and confirmation questions are ordinary prose. An ellipsis is one character (`…`), and
"Saving…" is the label of a button in progress; three dots are gone (`test/designSystemGuard.test.ts`).

## 2. The add verb is `Add`

`Add <thing>` on the trigger, `Add` on the modal's submit button. Never `Create`.

Detail and reasoning in [`ACTIONS_AND_MENUS.md`](ACTIONS_AND_MENUS.md) § 6 — the short version is
that the product had `Create role` and `Add office` on two tabs of one page, and a flow where the
reader pressed **Add office** and confirmed **Create**.

## 3. Two tab pairs need distinct names

A tab group whose title does not change must name **both** destinations, or the second tab is
unlabelled once you are on it.

| Route group | Problem | Rule |
|---|---|---|
| `/organization` — **People** · **Org Chart** | Had one fixed `h1` "Organisation" over both | The group needs a name that covers both, and each tab keeps its own distinct label |
| `/settings/general` — **Job Catalog** · **Job Levels** | The title stayed **"Job Catalog"** on the Job Levels tab, so the page claimed to be one of its own children | Same |

The legal-entities/offices group already does this correctly: **the title and description change per
tab**. That is the pattern to copy — and both pairs above now follow it, titling the page by the
active tab, so neither needed a group title.

What **is** settled: a tab's own label and its page title must not contradict each other, and one tab
of a pair may not borrow the other's name.

## 4. Organisation, one spelling

The sidebar said **Organization** and the page it opened was headed **Organisation** — American and
British spelling of the same word, one click apart. Elsewhere the app is American (`organization` in
the job-catalog and legal-entity copy).

Pick one and use it everywhere. Given the rest of the product, that is **`Organization`**.

## 5. Numbers, joiners, lists and balances

From the designers' home round (`hris/design/handoffs/2026-11-11-home/PRODUCT-RULES.md`), taken by the owner on 2026-11-11.

- **A number and its word never break apart**: "3 days", "14.5 vacation days" — a non-breaking space, or both in one
  `whitespace-nowrap` element.
- **"joins", never "joined"**, for a new joiner on their first day or before it.
- **"pending"** for something waiting on the reader ("2 pending") — not "documents" or "need your signature".
- **The link to a whole list says "See all", or names the list**: "All documents", "All processes", "My time off",
  "Calendar", "Inbox". Never a repeat of the card's own title ("All automations" under *Automations*).
- **A balance shows what is left**, never "of N" or "used"; a type with no limit says **"No limit"**.
- **A birthday never shows a year.**

## What this does not settle

- Whether `Delete forever` (documents trash) stays distinct from `Delete`.
- The select placeholder verbs — see [`FORMS_AND_FIELDS.md`](FORMS_AND_FIELDS.md).
